Epicurus on life

Epicurus (341–270 BCE) approaches life within Epicureanism. Pleasure is tranquil freedom from bodily distress and mental disturbance, achieved through modest desires, friendship, and atomist understanding. Systematically, the teaching links pleasure, atoms, friendship into a practical and theoretical whole. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets life most directly—useful for searches such as “epicurus quotes on life.”

How to use this page

Start with the shortest passage, then compare tone across sources. Return to the Epicurus thinker page for biography and to the life theme for other voices on the same question.
